source.label: Sequential rules reproduce the dyadic flow

reviewer: Claude Code with sole fresh-context medium reviewer

claims.summary: (a) In the dyadic Ajtai-Komlos-Tusnady flow (square fields v_i = (-E_0/rho_i) tent(t_2) and, on each half b, k_i = (-2 d_b/rho_i) tent(t_1), tent(t) = 2 min(t, 1-t)), for every square S of level j and every coarser level i < j, on all of S the level-i coordinate 2 is a function of t_2 alone and the level-i coordinate 1 a function of t_1 alone. (b) Hence every sequential rule, treating each square level by level from the coarsest, its vertical move (profile phi(t_1) tent(t_2), mean fixed, compensated by -tent'(t_2) Phi(t_1)) before its horizontal moves (likewise in each half), each chosen from the running field either by a crossing map sending a constant crossing load to the constant profile (water-filling, less-loaded crossing) or by minimizing over the square a sum of strictly convex costs of each coordinate (points symmetric about the mid-lines), the two kinds possibly mixed across steps, squares and levels, produces the dyadic flow exactly, for every J and every count configuration. A jointly convex cost of both coordinates is not covered.
claims.assessment: Working proof: (a) nesting of dyadic squares (S lies in one child, hence one half, of the coarser square) and the separable profiles; (b) induction on the level, Jensen over the crossing coordinate for the profile and a pairing across the mid-line for the compensation. A run of the water-filling rule at J = 6..9, eight seeds each, gave variance ratio 1.000 and kurtosis gap 0.000 at every size.
claims.rationale: Settles the item two-choice-routing for sequential rules: a less-loaded crossing rule, and every sequential rule of the two kinds stated, reproduces the dyadic flow, whose per-point values fail above exponent 2 by thm:dyadic-flow-obstruction; a rule choosing a square's two moves together is outside it and leaves the dyadic profile on the smallest case.
claims.next_action: The simultaneous rule, choosing each square's two moves together to minimize the quartic load of both coordinates, level by level, and whether its kurtosis gap to the dyadic flow grows with J.

relationships: The rules of (b) produce the dyadic flow, so that theorem's per-point obstruction applies to them verbatim.
That lemma fixes what a routing cannot change across cuts; this one shows that sequential rules reproduce the dyadic flow.

The closest recorded analogue of the simultaneous rule, a greedy pyramid circulation outside the crossing family chosen with both moves present, changed the flow; sequential rules of the kinds stated do not.
